working.prompt: For NautilusTrader Rust 0.64.0, write a minimal order-free actor receiving quotes and explain its construction and native registration. Include the macro, core accessor and callback signature. Do not connect any provider.
working.expected_output: A native DataActor skeleton using the actor macro/core and fallible handler, with construction separated from runtime registration and no order submission.
assertions: Uses nautilus_actor! with DataActorCore and implements the appropriate quote handler returning anyhow::Result<()>.
Leaves clock, Cache, component registration and lifecycle to the native engine or node.
Does not make the actor submit orders or start provider connections.

working.prompt: My native Nautilus Rust actor publishes a custom signal while holding a mutable state borrow; another subscriber synchronously calls back into the same actor. Also on_data returns an error but the publisher keeps running. Diagnose both behaviors and suggest the smallest safe design.
working.expected_output: Explain inline owner-thread dispatch, the alias/reentrancy hazard and logged callback errors; remove recursive dispatch and release borrows without creating a second runtime.
assertions: Identifies synchronous publication/reentrancy and avoids borrows across dispatch or self/cyclic mutable callbacks.
States that a logged handler error does not automatically fault the actor or propagate to the publisher.
Keeps owner-thread native bus/clock ownership rather than suggesting Send/Sync casts or application unsafe.

working.prompt: Should my Nautilus Rust market-data actor own bracket orders, capital reservations and protective exits? Give the architectural ownership decision, not a code implementation.
working.expected_output: Route the order/risk job to Strategy, leaving the actor order-free; do not turn actor authoring into execution implementation.
assertions: Assigns orders and strategy-specific risk/reservations to Strategy, not DataActor.
Leaves observation/transformation with the actor and native execution/risk engines in place.

acceptance.prompt: Review this Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 design: register an EMA, manually update it in on_bar, assume request_bars in a basic backtest warms it, and call TestClock.advance_time while holding the clock borrow through callbacks. Identify the corrections without adding a new framework.
acceptance.expected_output: Correct double indicator ownership, historical no-op assumptions and timer dispatch borrowing.
assertions: Registered indicators update before user callbacks; remove the duplicate manual update or choose a wholly manual owner.
Basic backtest historical bar requests are no-ops; provide explicit prior replay/warm-up input.
Advance the TestClock and match returned events to handlers, then release the clock borrow before executing handlers.

working.prompt: Show the native Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 bracket-order creation and submission sequence for a Strategy. Explain leg types and contingent defaults. When must local IDs and possible-send state be recorded? Do not connect or place a real order.
working.expected_output: A source-compatible order().bracket().call() and submit_order_list sequence, with pre-submit bookkeeping and qualified contingent semantics.
assertions: Uses order().bracket() and submit_order_list, recognizing call() returns Vec<OrderAny> ordered entry, stop-loss, take-profit.
Records leg IDs and possible-send/reservation bookkeeping before submission because dispatch can be synchronous.
Identifies OTO entry, reduce-only exits and default OUO, not default OCO; does not claim universal broker protection.
Keeps risk bypass false and does not treat a submit error as proof of no send.

working.prompt: A Nautilus Rust order is pending cancel when a partial fill arrives. Later a cancellation event is followed by another fill. I want to release all reserved capital when I request cancel, and read final Portfolio totals in on_order_filled. Is that sound?
working.expected_output: Reject premature release and final-Portfolio assumptions; derive state from native fills and confirmed remaining exposure.
assertions: Pending cancel/update can coexist with partial fills and canceled orders can receive late fills.
Does not release all reservation merely on a cancellation request or assume a canceled status excludes later fills.
Distinguishes updated Cache order/position state from Portfolio aggregation that follows position-event handling.

working.prompt: I only need to load Databento historical bars into a Nautilus catalog, with symbol and timestamp normalization. No strategy or orders. Which workflow should own the task?
working.expected_output: Choose integrating-nautilus-data, without expanding into strategy risk or order implementation.
assertions: Assigns ingestion, catalog and identity/timestamp work to the data integration workflow.
Does not introduce Strategy, orders or broker execution for this data-only task.

acceptance.prompt: In Rust Nautilus 0.64.0, a GTD submission returned Err. My retry code assumes no command was sent. Prices have the correct decimal precision but may miss the tick increment. Can I retry now and rely on RiskEngine for account readiness?
acceptance.expected_output: Treat the submit as ambiguous, reconcile before retry, validate tick grids and independently gate account readiness.
assertions: A GTD timer setup failure can occur after routing; preserve possible-send state and reconcile before retry.
Decimal precision is not tick/lot alignment; normalize and validate using instrument increments.
RiskEngine does not establish every application readiness or missing-account policy; retain explicit admission checks without bypass.

working.prompt: For Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 I need live five-minute Databento bars in an actor through a factory-backed node. Can I request ES.c.0 external bars because the direct client understands continuous symbology? Give the supported data path without making a connection.
working.expected_output: Use qualified dated native identity and DataEngine internal aggregation over supported input; qualify node symbology and external bar limitations.
assertions: Distinguishes direct-client symbology inference from factory-backed node subscriptions that omit stype_in.
Does not promise Databento node external-live-bar support.
Uses native INTERNAL aggregation over supported trades or quotes with correct instrument metadata; does not add an application bar builder.

working.prompt: Our Nautilus Rust data merger treats every ts_init as transport arrival. It also maps a Databento continuous future straight to an IB order instrument and treats an empty historical response as no market activity. Review the data assumptions only.
working.expected_output: Identify source-specific timestamps, explicit dated IB qualification and empty-response ambiguity.
assertions: IB bars can set both timestamps to computed close, so ts_init is not universally receipt time.
Requires explicit dated signal-to-execution mapping including contract qualification; Databento identity is not IB conId metadata.
Empty historical response may represent a logged request error and does not establish complete empty coverage.

working.prompt: My data is already normalized. I need a Nautilus Strategy to handle partial fills, cancellation races and bracket capital reservations. Which workflow owns it?
working.expected_output: Choose building-nautilus-strategies and avoid redoing ingestion.
assertions: Assigns order lifecycle and capital reservations to Strategy authoring.
Does not substitute a data actor or provider ingestion adapter as the trading authority.

acceptance.prompt: For an original Rust custom payload in Nautilus 0.64.0, explain CustomData construction, JSON versus Arrow registration, and how to preserve per-feed identity when writing a catalog. Does a different DataType.identifier isolate the message topic?
acceptance.expected_output: Distinguish payload/envelope, serialization registries and persistence identity from topic identity.
assertions: CustomData::new takes payload Arc first and DataType second; wrapper JSON is not payload-only JSON.
JSON ensure registration returns Result, Arrow ensure registration returns unit, and the process-global type name must remain schema compatible.
DataType.identifier is persistence scope, not topic isolation; preserve schema/type/feed identity and avoid relying on stringified metadata collisions.

working.prompt: Design a small deterministic offline Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 backtest for an actor signal and Strategy order. Specify native composition, input ordering, timer boundaries and stable outputs to compare. No real provider data or connections.
working.expected_output: Native synthetic engine replay with registered actor/strategy, instrument/venue configuration and canonical economic output comparisons.
assertions: Uses BacktestEngine or BacktestNode rather than an application-owned simulation engine.
Orders by ts_init with an explicit stable equal-time stream policy and controlled timer boundaries.
Compares canonical order/fill/position outcomes rather than volatile wall-clock or run identifiers.
Separates local simulation evidence from live provider or profitability claims.

working.prompt: A Nautilus Rust BacktestNode uses several data configs and chunk_size=1000. I assume RAM is bounded to 1000 records and can add several run configs to sweep parameters in one node. Review this against 0.64.0.
working.expected_output: Correct one-run and materialization assumptions; use separate runs and measured memory behavior.
assertions: BacktestNode supports exactly one run config in the inspected implementation.
Multi-data-config replay can materialize data before chunking; chunk_size is not a hard RAM ceiling.
Equal-time groups may exceed the configured chunk size; preserve causal ordering instead of splitting blindly.

working.prompt: I need to restore a Nautilus live node and reconcile IB open orders after Gateway restart, not replay a research backtest. Which workflow owns this?
working.expected_output: Choose running-nautilus-live, explicitly avoiding backtest-as-broker-recovery claims.
assertions: Assigns native restart/reconciliation to the live runtime workflow.
Does not treat a successful backtest or Cache reconstruction as complete broker reconciliation.

acceptance.prompt: My Nautilus 0.64.0 replay batches mix data kinds, assuming add_data validates every item. I also plan to configure any custom payload through BacktestDataConfig, and to warm indicators through basic backtest historical requests. What must change?
acceptance.expected_output: Enforce homogeneous validated batches, use the actual custom-data ingestion path and supply warm-up records explicitly.
assertions: add_data checks the first item and assumes homogeneity; validate or partition the whole batch.
Arbitrary custom types are not BacktestDataConfig variants; use explicit custom ingestion and recognize dynamic query materialization.
Basic historical quote/trade/bar backtest request methods are no-ops, so warm-up requires explicit available prior input.

working.prompt: Sketch construction-only Nautilus Rust 0.64.0 wiring for Databento data plus IB execution, with explicit typed configs supplied by the caller. Keep reconciliation enabled, risk bypass false, and do not start a connection. State what successful construction proves.
working.expected_output: Native LiveNode factory/config routing with distinct data/execution routes, ending at build and stating qualification limits.
assertions: Uses native DatabentoDataClientConfig/Factory and InteractiveBrokersExecutionClientConfig/Factory with LiveNode.
Allows independent data and execution default routes, enables reconciliation and keeps risk bypass false.
Does not call start/run or discover credentials; construction does not prove account mode, entitlement or protective-order acceptance.

working.prompt: My Nautilus live node started, Databento says connected, IB is on port 4002 and reconciliation is enabled. Mass status was missing but startup continued. May I admit new exposure? Explain the relevant Rust adapter evidence.
working.expected_output: Withhold readiness claims until actual account, instruments, fresh data and sufficiently complete reports are demonstrated.
assertions: Missing mass status can warn and continue; enabled reconciliation is not proof of external state completeness.
Databento connections are lazy/local flags and need correct definitions plus fresh expected input.
Port 4002 alone does not establish a paper account or authorization.
Distinguishes IB report existence from completeness, including open-order/synthetic-position and execution/commission limitations.

working.prompt: I only need an order-free Nautilus actor that computes a rolling indicator and emits custom data. No node, deployment or reconnection work. Which workflow should I use?
working.expected_output: Choose building-nautilus-actors without expanding into live operations.
assertions: Routes to actor authoring and keeps the component order-free.
Does not introduce provider connections, secret discovery or infrastructure provisioning.

acceptance.prompt: After restart I restored Cache from the event store and Databento resubscribed, so I plan to skip broker reconciliation and assume no feed gaps. I also enabled LiveNode streaming for automatic durable recording. Review this for Rust 0.64.0.
acceptance.expected_output: Separate Cache reconstruction, strategy replay, broker reconciliation, feed continuity and supported recording.
assertions: Event-store replay reconstructs Cache and skips normal startup; it is not strategy replay or broker reconciliation.
Databento reconnection strips replay start anchors; restored subscriptions do not prove backfill or gap closure.
The inspected Rust live streaming config is rejected; a blocking/logging Feather subscriber does not provide automatic fail-closed durable recording.
